T0 text patterns kept as data, not code literals, so the linter's own source cannot match itself (closes RT-10/RT-11).
The one place the tree is read; assays receive a manifest snapshot never a filesystem, and the tree is re-read at run-end to detect movement mid-run.
Minimal PNG decoder (8-bit, colour types 0/2/6, no interlace) that raises rather than guessing outside scope, so two captures are compared as decoded pixels, not base64 text.
Stands up and pins a renderer, handing back a page whose every wait is an in-page settling predicate, never a millisecond sleep.
Assembles the report in fixed order (counts first) and computes the headline word from the counts, with no branch where an author picks a different word.
Owns the denominator, the empty-population meaning, and single-write-per-id enforcement, so an assay cannot build its own population, redefine empty, or overwrite a result.
Fixed corpus run through the real, imported rig modules (not a re-description), so breaking the shipped rig by one line changes the probe's answer.
The five reading-verdict words and six run-exit codes, enumerated rather than folded, so two distinct states cannot collapse onto one number.
WebSocket client written against RFC 6455 with node builtins only (client-side text/continuation/ping-pong/close), handling all three CDP frame-length widths for multi-megabyte screenshots.

Census-diff gate for this registry itself: every source file under the five scanned directories has exactly one row, every row points at a file that still exists, no path has two rows, and `docs/sem_registry.json` is FRESH; `--self-test` fires all four failure directions (MISSING/STALE/DUPLICATE-adjacent/JSON-drift) red-first before the real run is trusted.

Parses this registry's four-column tables into `docs/sem_registry.json`, stamping the registry text's SHA-256 as `source_sha256` so `tools/sem_registry_gate.mjs` can report FRESH/STALE/ABSENT without re-deriving the parse by hand.
T0 tier: text-only evidence readings over rig-supplied entries (never touches the filesystem itself); patterns come from `lint-patterns.json`, never inline literals.
T1 tier: proves a module is live by evaluating (importing) it, not by pattern-matching its text.
T2 tier: mounts on a real DOM and asks "did anything appear at all" before asking whether it broke.
T3 tier: three independent pixel readings (ink-box overlap, used glyph size, baseline-ink diff against a committed picture); none reads the stylesheet.
The sole entry point allowed to print a verdict for the whole tree; runs self-check first, then every stage in fixed order, writes one JSON report; exit code is the `rig/verdict.mjs` state machine.
